answer: Here is one mechanism that works: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because orchard only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. In practice inlet is enforced by the ledger itself: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any mirror approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
